question: Radiation-related carcinogenesis is a stochastic effect, meaning there is no safe threshold dose below which the risk is zero.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Stochastic effects (carcinogenesis, hereditary effects) have no threshold; the probability of harm increases with dose but no dose is entirely risk-free — the basis for careful screening before ionising investigations.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Stochastic effects such as carcinogenesis follow a linear no-threshold model — any dose carries some probability of harm, which is why pregnancy and paediatric screening are mandatory before ionising radiation.
